text:
Closest recent match: [TiSRec, RecSys 2025](https://recsys.acm.org/recsys25/accepted-contributions/) dynamically segments histories into Local Preference Blocks using significant time intervals, then models preferences within and across blocks. Its abstract supports adaptive segmentation over fixed inactivity thresholds, but does not establish strictly causal boundary decisions or convolutional resets. [Parameter-Efficient Session Information, 2025](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109) explores session tokens, segment embeddings and temporal attention—lightweight session-conditioning alternatives, rather than learned change-point detection. No directly matching 2024–2026 boundary-reset NextItNet method was verified.

A practical foundational mechanism is [HM-RNN](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.01704v7): learned binary boundaries trigger UPDATE/COPY/FLUSH operations; straight-through gradients and slope annealing train discrete gates. Transfer the boundary concept into NextItNet without adopting its recurrent backbone. Caution: [PRIDES, 2025](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10976648) highlights recurring interests, supporting selective retention, but explicitly uses subsequent interactions to identify recurrence; that mechanism cannot be copied into strictly causal boundary decisions.

Proposed adaptation, not a published result: predict boundary probability b_t from observed prefix features—current/previous embeddings, their difference, and log timestamp gap. Attenuate each causal dilated-convolution tap from s to t by ε+(1−ε)∏_{u=s+1}^t(1−b_u). Apply at every temporal convolution; gating only the final output leaves earlier context mixed inside intermediate features. Keep residual connections within the same jointly trained network. Start with soft gates and low boundary bias; use a weak boundary-rate prior to discourage always-open/always-reset collapse, and monitor gate saturation and effective context length. Use prefix-only gate features, mask padding, and read the final nonpadding position.
